If you’re using a shared device and don’t want Firefox to remember your passwords, you change your preferences in the settings.
{note}We recommend that each person who shares a device should [[Access Mozilla services with a Mozilla account|create a Mozilla account]] and sign out every time, to prevent their logins from being exposed.

You can also use a [[Use a Primary Password to protect stored logins and passwords|Primary Password]] for additional protection.{/note}

=Disable all password saving=
#[[Template:optionspreferences]]
#Click {for not fx152}{menu Privacy & Security}{/for}{for fx152}{menu Passwords and autofill}{/for} in the panel to the left.
#{for not fx152}Scroll down to the ''Passwords'' section and{/for}{for fx152}In the ''Passwords'' section,{/for} uncheck the box next to ''Ask to save passwords''.
#;{for not fx152}[[Image:Passwords panel - not simplified]]{/for}{for fx152}[[Image:fx152asksavepassword]]{/for}<!-- (need Mac & Linux screenshots) -->
{/for}

=Disable password saving for specific websites only=
You can also configure Firefox not to save passwords for specific websites. To add these exceptions:
#[[Template:optionspreferences]]
#Click {for not fx152}{menu Privacy & Security}{/for}{for fx152}{menu Passwords and autofill}{/for} in the panel to the left.
#{for not fx152}Scroll down to the ''Passwords'' section and{/for}{for fx152}In the ''Passwords'' section,{/for} check the box next to ''Ask to save passwords''.
#Click {for not fx152}{menu Exceptions…} next to{/for}{for fx152}{menu Manage password exceptions} underneath{/for} ''Ask to save passwords'' to open the exceptions panel.
#;[[Image:Exceptions - saved passwords]] 
#Type the address of each website you don't want Firefox to save passwords, then click {button Block}.<br>Both http and https URLs for the website will be added to the exception list.
#You can use {button Remove Website} to remove the selected URL from the list, or {button Remove All Websites} to remove all exceptions.
#Click [[Image:Save changes button|width=120]]
